# Waste2Resource

> Australian engineering-led knowledge hub for tailings reuse, mine-waste valorisation and circular infrastructure.

## Core pages
- [Technical Library](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/): 30 source-linked case records with maturity and uncertainty.
- [Assessment Framework](https://waste2resource.com.au/assessment-framework/): site-specific decision path.
- [Research](https://waste2resource.com.au/research/): research summaries and evidence landscape.
- [Business Case](https://waste2resource.com.au/business-case/): value, cost, risk and closure screening.
- [Evidence Methodology](https://waste2resource.com.au/methodology/): editorial and maturity method.
- [About](https://waste2resource.com.au/about/): purpose, independence and scope.

## Case records
- [Plombières tailings in facing bricks](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/plombieres-bricks/): Untreated historic tailings were incorporated into facing-brick blends and assessed for product quality, environmental performance and lifecycle impacts. Source states: The study reports that untreated Plombières tailings produced compliant facing-brick blends, with the 40 wt% blend outperforming standard bricks in its lifecycle assessment.
- [Nador iron tailings in fired clay bricks](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/nador-fired-bricks/): Iron-mine tailings from an inactive operation were evaluated as an additive in red-clay fired bricks. Source states: Specimens containing 60% tailings reached 1.25 MPa compressive strength and had greater porosity than the reference bricks.
- [Pamaka cement–tailings masonry bricks](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/pamaka-bricks/): Artisanal gold-mining waste was tested in cement-bound bricks intended for non-loadbearing masonry. Source states: The tested bricks met non-loadbearing masonry standards, with compressive strengths of 5.02–13.3 MPa and total mercury of 0.03–0.10 mg/kg.
- [Southern Ecuador gold tailings in concrete blocks](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/ecuador-blocks/): Gold tailings were assessed as a partial sand substitute in concrete-block manufacture. Source states: Blocks replacing 50% or 70% of sand passed the reported leaching criteria, but their compressive strength and absorption did not meet the applicable regulations.
- [WA iron-ore tailings geopolymer bricks](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/wa-geopolymer-bricks/): Western Australian iron-ore tailings were used as the principal feedstock in alkali-activated geopolymer bricks. Source states: The optimum geopolymer brick reached 50.53 MPa unconfined compressive strength and met the cited Australian and ASTM brick requirements.
- [Mina do Pico tailings block factory](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/pico-block-factory/): Vale operates a block plant that converts sandy iron-ore tailings into interlocking pavers and other precast products. Source states: Vale reports that the Pico plant has converted tailings into interlocking pavers since 2021 and produced more than 407,000 pavers in 2025.
- [Donimalai iron tailings masonry units](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/donimalai-bricks/): Donimalai tailings were tested with cement, sand and sodium silicate in brick formulations. Source states: The 8:2 tailings-to-cement mix reached 8.58 MPa, while the more economical 9:1 mix complied with the cited Indian brick standard.
- [WA tailings and waste rock in mine shotcrete](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/wa-shotcrete/): A University of Western Australia programme is investigating mine wastes as aggregate and partial binder inputs for underground shotcrete. Source states: The funded project aims to replace conventional shotcrete aggregate with tailings and waste rock and to reduce cement demand; the project page does not report performance results.
- [Shuangqi gold tailings glass-ceramics](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/shuangqi-glass-ceramic/): Gold tailings were used at high content in dense glass-ceramics produced through controlled heat treatment. Source states: At 60 wt% tailings and 950°C for two hours, the glass-ceramic reached 116 MPa flexural strength and 8.17 GPa hardness.
- [Spodumene tailings in building ceramics](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/finland-lithium-ceramics/): Quartz–feldspar tailings and waste glass wool were co-processed into high-performance ceramic specimens. Source states: The tailings and glass-wool ceramics met ASTM C62 requirements and reached 90 MPa compressive strength and 25 MPa flexural strength.
- [Century zinc tailings retreatment](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/century-zinc/): A large-scale hydraulic mining and flotation operation recovers zinc from the former Century Mine tailings deposit. Source states: The operator describes Century as Australia's largest tailings retreatment operation and reports hydraulic re-mining of the zinc-bearing tailings storage facility.
- [Mount Morgan tailings processing and rehabilitation](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/mount-morgan/): The project is designed to recover value from historic tailings while funding rehabilitation of a major legacy mine site. Source states: NAIF reports financial close on a loan of up to A$66 million for a project intended to recover gold and copper while rehabilitating the legacy mine site.
- [Hellyer polymetallic tailings reprocessing](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/hellyer/): The Hellyer facility has reprocessed legacy polymetallic tailings to produce precious- and base-metal concentrates. Source states: Tasmania's EPA reported that tailings reprocessing began in 2018 to produce lead, zinc and pyrite concentrates, with residual tailings placed in a new storage facility.
- [Ergo gold tailings retreatment](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/ergo/): Historic Witwatersrand tailings are reclaimed and treated through a large surface gold-recovery network. Source states: DRDGOLD reports that Ergo hydraulically reclaims historic slimes and treats them through screening, classification, milling and carbon-in-leach recovery.
- [El Teniente tailings copper recovery](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/mvc-chile/): Minera Valle Central recovers copper and molybdenum from fresh El Teniente tailings and historic deposits. Source states: MVC states that it processes all fresh El Teniente tailings and also hydraulically reclaims historic tailings to produce copper and molybdenum concentrates.
- [Missouri cobalt and nickel tailings recovery](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/missouri-cobalt/): Legacy tailings were evaluated and reprocessed for cobalt-bearing and nickel-bearing concentrates alongside closure works. Source states: ITRC reports that a tailings processing facility was built in 2019 to recover cobalt-bearing concentrates before sampling and covering the remaining material.
- [Pine Creek secondary critical-mineral prospectivity](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/pine-creek-miwatch/): Government-led sampling is assessing historic Pine Creek wastes as potential secondary resources for critical and precious metals. Source states: The first-pass Cosmo study found anomalous silver, gold and arsenic and proposed flotation, gravity, cyanidation and bioleaching for further investigation.
- [Kunwarara tailings to magnesium feedstock](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/kunwarara-magnesium/): QMAG is characterising fine tailings for fractions suitable for high-purity magnesium chloride and magnesium-metal production. Source states: The Queensland program will characterise and test fine magnesite tailings to identify fractions suitable for high-purity magnesium-chloride feedstock.
- [Kidston direct tailings revegetation](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/kidston-revegetation/): Field work assessed whether the tailings surface could support vegetation directly without a conventional soil cap. Source states: The paper reports that alkaline tailings supported native trees and shrubs without a soil cap when establishment included initial irrigation and fertilisation.
- [Sudbury amended-tailings Technosols](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/sudbury-technosol/): Mine residuals were blended with pulp-and-paper residues and forest humus to create plant-growth substrates. Source states: Organic amendments increased pH, germination and plant growth, but soluble copper and nickel also increased in some amended substrates.
- [Fine-coal tailings Technosols](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/coal-technosol-sa/): Fine coal wastes and organic amendments were evaluated as engineered soils for mine-site rehabilitation. Source states: The report found one ultrafine coal-waste stream unsuitable for soil manufacture, while two other streams supported coal recovery and experimental Technosol development.
- [Wheal Jane mine-water treatment](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/wheal-jane/): A long-running active scheme manages high-flow contaminated water from the former mine after passive pilot trials. Source states: The operating scheme treats about 5.6 million cubic metres of mine water annually using lime dosing, aeration, sludge recirculation and clarification.
- [Tailings-containing adsorbents screened for mine-water treatment](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/finland-reactive-barrier/): Mine-tailings-containing alkali-activated adsorbents were screened in laboratory tests, but the field pilot used a slag-only formulation. Source states: Mine-tailings-containing adsorbents were screened in laboratory work, but the one-week field pilot used the selected slag-only adsorbent rather than a tailings-containing formulation.
- [Mount Keith nickel-tailings carbonation](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/mount-keith-carbon/): Weathering of reactive ultramafic tailings forms stable carbonate minerals, with field programmes examining acceleration and verification. Source states: The model reproduced carbonate minerals observed in ten-year-old tailings and estimated passive carbon uptake of 0.6–1 kg CO₂ per square metre per year.
- [Crawford in-process tailings carbonation](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/crawford-carbonation/): A pilot programme is integrating CO₂ mineralisation into the proposed nickel process and tailings circuit. Source states: The active government-funded project aims to demonstrate pilot-scale storage and permanence; future million-tonne claims depend on the proposed mine becoming operational.
- [SCO2UT ultramafic-tailings field research](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/sco2ut-canada/): A multi-site programme investigates accelerated carbon mineralisation and verification methods across different residues and climates. Source states: The research program is testing ways to accelerate carbon mineralisation, verify storage stability and integrate field trials into mine operations.
- [Iron tailings in an experimental pavement section](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/brazil-road-section/): Tailings, waste rock and iron-ore canga were placed in base and sub-base mixtures in a monitored experimental road section. Source states: The 35% tailings mixtures behaved differently in the field, and cracking and deformation appeared within a year; the authors recommend more conservative proportions.
- [Tanami gold-tailings cemented paste backfill](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/tanami-paste-backfill/): Dry excavated tailings are conditioned and pumped underground as cemented paste backfill at the Tanami gold operation. Source states: The case study reports that a chemical admixture increased solids content, reduced pipeline pressure and improved throughput and strength consistency for excavated tailings paste.
- [Bowen Basin coal-tailings critical-mineral study](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/bowen-coal-critical-minerals/): A regional programme is examining rare earths, vanadium and broader value-recovery options in coal mine tailings across the Bowen Basin. Source states: The A{id:'bowen-coal-critical-minerals',title:'Bowen Basin coal-tailings critical-mineral study',location:'Bowen Basin, Queensland, Australia',region:'Asia-Pacific',material:'Tailings',commodity:'Metallurgical and thermal coal',waste:'Coal mine tailings',pathway:'Metals recovery',stage:'Regional study',readiness:'Early research',evidence:'Queensland Government-funded programme',lat:-22.2,lng:148.2,summary:'A regional programme is examining rare earths, vanadium and broader value-recovery options in coal mine tailings across the Bowen Basin.',technical:'The funded work is intended to characterise multiple waste streams and screen recovery and full-volume reuse pathways with participating producers and research partners.',environmental:'No recovery performance is yet established publicly. - [NSW mine-waste critical-mineral characterisation](https://waste2resource.com.au/technical-library/cases/nsw-mine-reuse/): More than 1,200 samples from 28 mine sites and one power-station site were screened for critical minerals and high-tech metals. Source states: The program analysed more than 1,200 samples from 28 mine sites and found elevated concentrations of 11 critical minerals, including copper, cobalt, silver and antimony.

Content is informational and does not replace site investigation, approvals or engineering advice.
